description.value: A pilot study examined electrophysiological correlates of real-time fMRI neurofeedback training by combining simultaneous passive EEG recordings with rtfMRI in unmedicated patients with major depressive disorder.

spans.text: We report the first study investigating electrophysiological correlates of the rtfMRI-nf procedure, by combining the rtfMRI-nf with simultaneous and passive EEG recordings.

value: we hypothesized that the participants receiving the amygdala-based rtfMRI-nf would show positive FEA changes during the rtfMRI-nf task, indicating an enhancement in approach motivation, compared to control participants receiving a sham rtfMRI-nf.
we hypothesized that FEA variations during the rtfMRI-nf task targeting the amygdala would exhibit a temporal correlation with the simultaneously measured BOLD activity of the amygdala.

source_definition.value: Interaction between the left-prefrontal upper-alpha EEG power regressor, defined as the average of normalized powers from channels F3, F7, and FC5 and convolved with the hemodynamic response function, and the Happy Memories-minus-Count task contrast; it measured task-dependent temporal correlation between this EEG regressor and BOLD activity.

model_settings.value: Voxelwise GLM-based psychophysiological interaction analysis. FEA time series were converted to z-scores, convolved with an 8-ms-resolution hemodynamic response function, subsampled at middle time points of fMRI volumes, linearly detrended, and entered as PPI correlation and Happy-minus-Count interaction regressors. fMRI data and motion parameters were band-pass filtered from 0.01 to 0.1 Hz. The design matrix included four stimulus regressors, ten nuisance covariates including motion, CSF, white-matter, and power-sum PPI regressors, and five polynomial baseline terms. Maps were spatially smoothed with a 5-mm FWHM kernel and normalized using Fisher r-to-z transformation.
